neighbours.label: ' order' in the purpose idiom 'in order to' (not the noun order)
fire: The bakers rise before dawn in order to have fresh bread by six.
Several lanes were closed in order to repair the bridge deck.
You must register early in order to get a seat at the workshop.
He sold his boat in order to pay for his daughter's tuition.
The club moved its meeting, in order that more members could attend.
They cut the price sharply in order to clear out the old stock.
Parents should read aloud in order to build a child's vocabulary.
We drained the tank in order to find the source of the leak.
quiet: The bakers rise before dawn so as to have fresh bread by six.
Several lanes were closed to repair the bridge deck.
You must register early for a seat at the workshop.
He sold his boat and paid for his daughter's tuition.
The club sent out the order for new chairs that members wanted.
They placed a large order with the supplier of the old stock.
Parents should read aloud because it builds a child's vocabulary.
We drained the tank and found the source of the leak.

notes: Max is only 4.47 and the gate-closed regime dominates. ' order' is 10 of the top 32; ' that' and others are weaker and not claimed here, so this will not cover the whole pole.
